### Page note: https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/en/notes-coins/notes-and-coins/history-of-currency-in-sri-lanka
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
**Page**  
Title: *History of Currency in Sri Lanka* – Central Bank of Sri Lanka  
URL: https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/en/notes-coins/notes-and-coins/history-of-currency-in-sri-lanka  

**Evidence**  
- “[Notes issued by the private banks, namely, (1844 – 1884) The Oriental Bank Corporation, The Chartered Mercantile Bank of India, London and China, Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation, Asiatic Banking Corporation (i) Pound notes (ii) Rupee notes]” – shows that foreign private banks issued banknotes in Sri Lanka during the 19th century.  
- “The Central Bank of Ceylon was established on 28th August 1950 in terms of the Monetary Law Act No. 58 of 1949.” – establishes the 20th century institutional framework for currency.  
- “From 1884 – 1950 the Board of Commissioners of Currency (Under Government of Ceylon) … issued subsidiary notes for the values of 5 cents, 10 cents, 25 cents, 50 cents and 1 rupee.” – indicates government‑issued notes in the late 19th‑mid‑20th century.  
- “Under the provisions of the Emergency Powers Acts. 1939 and 1940 the Board of Currency was authorized to issue denominations below one rupee to meet the shortage of coins.” – evidence of 20th‑century note‑issuance by a state body.  

**Coverage**  
The page provides complete evidence for:  

- **Foreign private banks** that issued banknotes in Sri Lanka in the 19th century (1844‑1884): Oriental Bank Corp., Chartered Mercantile Bank of India, HK & Shanghai Banking Corp., Asiatic Banking Corp.  
- **Introduction of the Central Bank of Ceylon** (established 28 Aug 1950).  
- **Board of Commissioners of Currency** and its subsidiary notes (1884‑1950).  
- **Emergency‑Powers‑Act‑era** subsidiary note issuance (1939‑1940).  

**Missing**  
The supplied page does **not** provide direct evidence for:  

1. A *concession* granted to a foreign bank to print its own banknotes in Sri Lanka during the 20th century.  
2. The specific year in which any such concession was granted.  
3. Details on 20th‑century foreign‑bank‑issued notes (if any existed).  

**Next links**  
1. https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/en/about/about-the-bank/history – likely to contain the history of the Central Bank and any foreign‑bank concessions in the 20th century.  
2. https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/en/about/about-the-bank/bank-history – potential source for foreign‑bank note‑printing agreements.  
3. https://www.cbsl.gov.lk/en/notes-coins/notes-and-coins/notes-issue-by-private-banks (if exists) – would directly address private‑bank note issuance and concessions.  

**Expand**: yes – these links are concrete routes that could establish the missing facts.
